steps.say: A proximal opening with hidden testes is never just a simple hypospadias, because sex development may be affected. Proximal hypospadias with cryptorchidism demands karyotype and disorder of sex development workup including mixed gonadal dysgenesis, partial androgen insensitivity and congenital adrenal hyperplasia in a virilised female. Five to 10 percent of proximal cases carry a dilated prostatic utricle.
steps.tx: Proximal **hypospadias** (under surface opening) with cryptorchidism demands **karyotype** (chromosome test) and **disorder of sex development** (DSD) workup including mixed gonadal dysgenesis, partial androgen insensitivity and congenital adrenal hyperplasia in a virilised female, and **5** to **10** percent of proximal cases carry a dilated prostatic utricle.

vis.alt: Penile diagrams showing hypospadias triad with ventral meatus, chordee and hooded prepuce beside epispadias with dorsal meatus.
vis.caption: Proximal hypospadias with cryptorchidism needs karyotype and DSD workup before repair. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Never cut the foreskin in hypospadias, because it is the spare part the repair is depending on. Circumcision must never remove the foreskin since it supplies repair tissue, and ideal repair age is 6 to 12 months. The tubularised incised plate with vascularised foreskin flap fixes most distal cases in one ambulatory operation.
steps.tx: **Circumcision** (foreskin removal) must never remove the foreskin in hypospadias since it supplies repair tissue, ideal repair age is **6** to **12** months, and the tubularised incised plate (**TIP repair**, slit and roll technique) with vascularised **foreskin flap** (pedicled cover) fixes most distal cases in one ambulatory operation.

vis.alt: Urinary diagrams showing hypospadias repair, urethral valve ablation, pyeloplasty with stent, and buccal mucosa graft rescue.
vis.caption: TIP repair with foreskin flap suits most distal cases as one ambulatory operation. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Parents must hear honest numbers, because trouble climbs steeply toward the back of the penis. Complications track severity at 5 percent distal, 10 percent midpenile and 40 percent proximal, led by urethrocutaneous fistula and meatal stenosis. Buccal mucosa graft rescue is helping complex redos heal.
steps.tx: Complications track severity at **5** percent distal, **10** percent midpenile and **40** percent proximal, led by **urethrocutaneous fistula** (skin leak) and **meatal stenosis** (narrow opening) with **buccal mucosa graft** (cheek lining) rescue for complex redos that keep leaking. Redo surgery is planned jointly with the family after full counselling.

steps.say: Bladder exstrophy spans from a split urethra to the whole cloaca lying open, and every case is leaking constantly. Bladder exstrophy occurs in about 1 in 35000 births spanning epispadias to cloacal exstrophy, and shows an exposed midline bladder with caudally displaced cord, wide scrotum and dorsal chordee epispadias in males. Untreated children remain totally incontinent.
steps.tx: **Bladder exstrophy** (open bladder plate) occurs in about 1 in **35000** births spanning **epispadias** (split upper urethra) to cloacal exstrophy, with exposed midline bladder, caudally displaced cord, wide scrotum and dorsal **chordee** ( upward bend) epispadias in males, leaving total incontinence untreated.

steps.say: Cover the open bladder with cling film at once, and keep latex away from this child forever. The bladder is covered with plastic wrap never gauze at birth, and latex allergy precautions run from nursery to theatre. Transfer goes to a specialist centre with paediatric urology and anaesthesia.
steps.tx: The bladder is covered with **plastic wrap** (cling film) never gauze at birth, and **latex allergy** (rubber reaction) precautions run from nursery to theatre. Transfer goes to a **specialist centre** (paediatric urology and anaesthesia unit), since results depend on experienced teams.

nodes.label: Plastic wrap cover, latex free care

steps.say: Closing the pelvis needs bone surgery first, then the bladder and urethra follow in stages. Most undergo bilateral iliac osteotomy to close the pubic symphysis, staged reconstruction closes the bladder first, fixes epispadias at 1 to 2 years and reconstructs the neck at 3 to 6 years once capacity reaches 80 to 90 millilitres. Single stage repair risks penile injury and hydronephrosis.
steps.tx: Most undergo bilateral iliac **osteotomy** (pelvic bone cut) to close the pubic symphysis, **staged reconstruction** (stepwise closure) closes the bladder first, fixes epispadias at **1** to **2** years and completes **bladder neck reconstruction** (outlet tightening) at **3** to **6** years once capacity reaches **80** to **90** mL with rectal sphincter control.

steps.say: Two thirds of well managed children achieve dryness, though the upper tracts need lifelong watching. Continence rate is reaching 60 to 70 percent in good centres with under 15 percent upper tract deterioration. Valsalva voiding using belly pressure empties the bladder since the neck never relaxes, and failures move to augmentation cystoplasty with stoma options.
steps.tx: **Continence rate** (dryness achieved) reaches **60** to **70** percent in good centres with under **15** percent upper tract deterioration. **Valsalva voiding** (belly pressure emptying) works since the neck never relaxes, and failures move to **augmentation cystoplasty** (bladder enlarging), continent stoma, artificial sphincter or ureterosigmoid diversion.

steps.say: Bowel joined to urine trades continence for lifelong risks that families must understand. Ureterosigmoidostomy risks chronic pyelonephritis, chloride and hydrogen absorption causing metabolic acidosis, and 15 to 22 percent long term colon carcinoma. Lifelong surveillance follows any intestinal urinary diversion with yearly scopes and labs.
steps.tx: **Ureterosigmoidostomy** (ureters to bowel) risks chronic pyelonephritis, chloride and hydrogen absorption causing **metabolic acidosis** (acid blood), and **15** to **22** percent long term **colon carcinoma** (bowel cancer). Lifelong surveillance follows any intestinal urinary diversion. Anaemia, growth failure and electrolyte shifts trigger earlier review.
